summary: Civilian Conservation Corps fire tower in Shenandoah National Park, built 1940-41 and since removed; a base and valley views remain on a 1.6-mile hike from Skyland.

facts.status_note: The tower is gone; a lookout base remains at the former site.

access.note: Reached on foot by the Millers Head Trail, which starts just up the hill from the Skyland amphitheater.

visit.trail_note: 1.6-mile round trip hike from the trailhead just up the hill from the Skyland amphitheater

events.note: Constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps and completed in 1941 (Willhite); Forest Lookouts gives 1942

evidence.quote: Millers Head Fire Tower was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1940, and completed in 1941.

evidence.supports: remaining lookout base at former site
viewpoint at site of former fire tower, reached on foot
evidence.quote: Take this hike to a spectacular viewpoint at the site of a former fire tower.

evidence.supports: trailhead just up the hill from Skyland amphitheater
evidence.quote: From the trailhead just up the hill from the Skyland amphitheater, take the Millers Head Trail to the viewpoint.

evidence.supports: view over the Shenandoah Valley from base

corrections.why: The record's built year is the completion year. Willhite says it was constructed in 1940 and completed in 1941, and Wikidata gives a 1940 start time.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite and Wikidata give 1940 construction with 1941 completion; Forest Lookouts gives 1942 construction. The disagreement is reported in the story and not settled here.

notes_for_editor: Built date disagrees: 1940 construction and 1941 completion (Willhite, Wikidata) against 1942 construction (Forest Lookouts). Status: FFLA and Forest Lookouts say gone or removed, while Willhite photographed a remaining base and Wikidata says ruinous; status_note records the base. No design, height, staffing or fire source was found. Coordinates match Wikidata to within a few metres. A Shenandoah NPS Facebook post (search snippet only, not read) gives the same 1940 and 1941 dates and mentions a remaining platform; it is not cited.
